# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [5]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[orange] 2:[blue] 3:[white] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the Deaf monkey. I can see the bomb but can't hear anything. I need to relay what I see to Mute (who can hear me and read the manual) so they can figure out the correct action, and Mute will need to relay instructions to Blind (who can't see or hear, only feel).

Since I'm last in speaking order (Blind, Mute, Deaf), whatever I send now will only be received at the start of next round. Let me report what I see clearly to Mute, since Mute can hear me.

I'll describe the display, light, and wires precisely so Mute can cross-reference with the manual.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Display shows 5. Light is yellow. Wires are 1 orange, 2 blue, 3 white, 4 green, 5 yellow.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [5]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[orange] 2:[blue] 3:[white] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

Mute gestured ✌ to me - that's two blanks worth of info I can see the shape but not what it means since gestures don't carry inherent meaning until established. Since Mute cannot speak, they're trying to signal something to me using gestures, which I *can* see.

This is likely Mute trying to establish a code, or acknowledge receipt, or ask a question. Since I don't yet have a shared vocabulary, I should keep reporting what I see and wait for a clearer pattern to emerge. Let me also acknowledge that I saw the gesture, but since I can't speak back in a way Mute would understand differently, I'll just continue relaying full info and see if Mute repeats or builds on this signal.

I'll restate the bomb details in case that first message didn't reach in time, and note I saw their gesture.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I saw your gesture, two marks. Confirming again: Display 5, Light yellow, Wires 1 orange 2 blue 3 white 4 green 5 yellow. Tell me what you need from me.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [5]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[orange] 2:[blue] 3:[white] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👍]

Mute is gesturing to me again: ✌ 👍. This could mean "wire 2, confirm/yes" - like Mute is telling me they identified wire 2 as the target based on the manual, and 👍 is confirmation/agreement, asking me to verify.

Since Mute can hear my speech but I can't hear theirs, and gestures are the only channel from Mute to me, they're likely trying to build a simple code: numbers via counting gestures, then a signal.

✌ could mean "2" (two fingers). 👍 could mean "correct/yes/confirm this is the one". So maybe Mute is confirming wire 2 (blue) is correct, or asking me if wire 2 matches something.

I should respond by speaking to Mute, confirming what wire 2 is, and asking if this is about which wire to cut, since Blind needs to act on wires.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Wire 2 is blue. If wire 2 is the one to cut, gesture thumbs up again to confirm. If not, gesture thumbs down.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [5]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[orange] 2:[blue] 3:[white] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute gestured 👍 alone this time - confirming my question. This suggests wire 2 (blue) is indeed the one to cut, based on the manual matching display=5, light=yellow.

But wait - I need to be careful. Mute cannot speak to Blind directly (Mute cannot speak at all). Mute can only gesture, and gestures only reach me (Deaf), not Blind. So Mute has no way to tell Blind which wire to cut except through me somehow, but I can't touch the bomb either.

Actually, re-reading: Blind speaks first, then Mute, then Deaf. I speak and Mute/Blind receive it. Mute gestures and only I receive it. So the only path from Mute's manual-knowledge to Blind's hands is: Mute gestures to me, I translate and speak to Blind (since Blind can hear me).

So I need to relay to Blind: cut wire 2. Let me confirm this is solid and then tell Blind directly.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Cut wire 2, the blue one.")
speak(to="mute", text="Confirmed, telling Blind to cut wire 2 now.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[CUT] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

Wire 2 was cut successfully and the bomb changed state - display now shows 1, light is purple, and wires have changed. This is a new stage requiring a new answer. I need to report this new state to Mute immediately so they can consult the manual again.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Success, bomb changed. New state: Display 1, Light purple. Wires now: 1 white, 2 CUT, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 orange.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[CUT] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

Mute gestured ☝ - one finger up, likely indicating "wire 1". Let me confirm with Mute before relaying to Blind, using the same pattern as before to be safe.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Wire 1 is white. Gesture thumbs up to confirm cut wire 1, thumbs down if not.")
```

TURN 7

LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[CUT] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Confirmed - wire 1 (white) is correct. Time to relay to Blind.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Cut wire 1, the white one.")
speak(to="mute", text="Confirmed, telling Blind to cut wire 1 now.")
```

WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[CUT] 3:[yellow] 4:[orange] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

Another success. Bomb changed again - display 1, light now red, wires updated. Report to Mute immediately.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Success, bomb changed again. New state: Display 1, Light red. Wires now: 1 CUT, 2 CUT, 3 yellow, 4 orange, 5 green.")
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[CUT] 3:[yellow] 4:[orange] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝]

Mute gestured three "one" symbols: ☝ ☝ ☝. This is different from before - could mean "wire 3" (three ones counted = 3), or it could be a repeated single gesture emphasizing something. Given the pattern so far used single gestures per digit position (✌ for 2, ☝ for 1), this new pattern of three ☝ symbols likely means "3" by tally/count rather than a single symbolic digit.

Let me confirm with Mute using the same verification pattern.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Do you mean wire 3? Wire 3 is yellow. Gesture thumbs up to confirm cut wire 3, thumbs down if not.")
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):

Confirmed - wire 3 (yellow). Relay to Blind.

```

speak(to="mute", text="Confirmed, telling Blind to cut wire 3 now.")
```

Success again! Only 2 wires left now: 4 (green) and 5 (orange). Report the new state to Mute.

```

```

Five ☝ gestures - following the tally pattern, this means wire 5. Let me confirm.
